task.description: WF-02 step 5, TEST-DESIGNER, the wording round of REQ-113 (run M1WORDS-20261122-02). In step 01 of this run FRONTEND-DEV, on ORCH's instruction, replaced the pinned values in the two test files together with the product texts (the rows (11) to (13) of the requirement's guard table) and added the table KK_DRAFT_VALUES to TX-4. By WF-02 the tests are yours; this step puts that change under your hand. Do, in this order: (1) Read the amended requirement and the diff of the two test files line by line. For every changed row: the pinned value equals the requirement's text exactly (compare by your own read-only script that takes the value from the requirement text, not from the product). (2) The new table KK_DRAFT_VALUES and its check in TX-4: is the oracle the test's own; does it compare the whole kk text; is «exactly one occurrence in texts.js» counted soundly (could it pass with a wrong text, with the text in a comment, with the text twice); is it red on the product of the base tag d1bfb93 (show it by a script that evaluates the same comparison on the module of the tag and on the module of the work). (3) Nothing is weakened: print the number of `test(` and `it(` calls and of `assert.` occurrences in each of the two files at the tag base/M1WORDS-20261122-02 and now (the number now is not lower); no skip, todo or only; the unit count stays 122 and the e2e count 15 unless you add a test (then say the new numbers). (4) Decide whether the amendment needs a new or a stronger assertion. Think by the class of error, not by these examples: a page that kept an old literal while the module changed (the result block, the how.html block, the four stage marks, the static Russian of how.html); the invitation sentence living outside the closing paragraph element or twice; the closing paragraph of four sentences in ru and en; the en mark shown anywhere as the old word; a kk draft leaking into the open build. If an existing test already goes red for the class, name the test and the assertion (file and line) and add nothing. If not, write the assertion in your two files by the conventions of the design's catalogue (own oracles; nothing imported from the product beyond what these files already import). A test that only looks for a word in a document is not written (Q6). (5) Mutants of the amendment, at least 14: each changed value mutated in a copy (ru now_idea_s back to the old text; the same without «(ТЗ)»; ru now_closing without the invitation sentence; the sentences in another order; en now_closing old; en stat_on «Works»; en now_idea_t old; en idea_panel_lead old; en demo_accuracy_note with «surer»; each kk draft changed by one letter; a kk draft twice in the module; the static Russian of how.html old for now_idea_s and for now_closing; two languages of one key swapped), and for each the test and the assertion that goes red. You cannot run the tests here: prove each mutant with your own script that applies it to a copy in your folder and evaluates the same comparison the test makes, and list in `result.must_be_proved_on_github` what only a run on GitHub can prove (ORCH plans one snapshot «the product of main with the tests of the work» that must be red). (6) Read the logs of the two GitHub runs (read-only: `gh run view <id> --log`) and write what they prove for the amended tests: TX-4, TX-9, TX-10 and LD-3, LD-6, LD-9 ran and passed, with the counts of each step. (7) Say plainly in `result.changes` whether you changed a test file: «no change» means the GitHub record above stands for step 6; a change means ORCH must send a new snapshot. You do not change product code; if a test needs a change of a product file, write it in `result.issues`. result.summary: Wording round of REQ-113, step 5. I checked the amended tests and found one real gap, which I closed with one new assertion in app/test/e2e/landing.test.js (no new test( call; counts unchanged: unit 122, e2e 15). (1) Pinned values: my read-only script took the 15 key pairs from the requirement paragraph «Words» and the two kk drafts from the amendment text, and compared them with the pinned tables of texts.test.js, with the module of the work and with the module of the tag d1bfb93: 32 rows, 0 differ from the requirement; exactly 9 differ from the base module, the nine values of the amendment (now_idea_t en, now_idea_s ru and kk, stat_on en, now_closing ru, en and kk, demo_accuracy_note en, idea_panel_lead en). landing.test.js holds no pinned product text: its diff against the tag is only the word Works to Working in two comments and three messages, and the page values come from the module through say(). (2) KK_DRAFT_VALUES: the table is a literal of the test file (no import, no call), the check compares the whole kk text with assert.equal, and counts the occurrences of the whole kk text in the source of texts.js (split on the text). The comparison is red on the module of the tag (both drafts: value and count) and green on the module of the work (count 1 each). I damaged the module in 19 ways (one letter, a look-alike Latin I, a trailing space, a dropped full stop, a no-break space, old text, sentences moved, the text twice as another value, in a comment on its own line, in a comment on the same line, value swapped with en or ru): 18 red; the one green case, K19 (the value written as two joined pieces and the whole text kept once in a comment), has the right value and one occurrence, so no wrong text and no leak passes: harmless and named. (3) Nothing weakened: test( calls 10 to 10 and 9 to 9, it( 0 and 0, assert. 93 to 96 (texts, unchanged file against the pre-step state; the rise is the amendment's) and 194 to 195 (landing, my new assertion), no skip, todo or only, every test title and order the same, LF only. (4) By the class of error the existing assertions already catch every class of the task except one: bare words in the status block that no element shape can see (a text node after the closing paragraph, between the heading and the list, or in a row). My mutants C03 (the invitation sentence as bare text after the closing paragraph of the result) and C06 (a bare word after the heading) stayed green in the stand-in of LD-6, because checkBlock compared the skeleton of elements only. I added to readBlock a TreeWalker over the text nodes of the block (field stray: every non-blank text node whose parent is not the h3, a span.stat, a b, a small or the closing paragraph) and to checkBlock one assertion «the status block holds its words and nothing more» (deepEqual with []); checkBlock runs for the result in ru/kk/en, the how.html block in ru/kk/en at two widths and with no script, and the held, retried and failed results, so one assertion guards all of them. It is not a word-in-a-document check: it fails on the page structure. (5) 43 mutants, one edit of a copy each, evaluated by my own script that cuts the real tables and the real checkBlock, checkHowPage, howFindings out of the test files and evaluates them on the damaged copy (stand-in page for the browser parts): 41 red before my change, 43 red after it, 0 green; on the product of the tag 11 failing assertions in TX-4 (the nine values, plus the two once-counts), on the product of the work none. (6) The GitHub record: workflow app run 45031353708 on 0c50fc2: job e2e success, 15 tests 15 pass, 0 skipped, 0 todo, with LD-3 (ok 3), LD-6 (ok 6) and LD-9 (ok 9) ok; job check step «Run the app check» success: unit 122 pass 0 fail 0 skipped 0 todo, with TX-4 (ok 98), TX-9 (ok 103) and TX-10 (ok 104) ok; int 47 pass; job pg 4 pass; job docker success. Workflow check run 45031353719 (the tools set): 2226 pass plus 9, 7, 13, 7, all 0 fail, 0 skipped, 0 todo (it does not run the app tests). That record covers the tests as they stood at 07a9759; it does not cover my new assertion. (7) I changed one test file: app/test/e2e/landing.test.js (+22 -1 lines against HEAD). So the GitHub record above does NOT stand for step 6 for that file: ORCH must send a new snapshot. texts.test.js is unchanged (sha256 8a417f0c...). No product file was touched.
